objective: Test whether the 17 CPVS residuals with both mean magnitudes and missing one band-specific period can be interpolated by a bounded, source-informed multiband Gaussian Process diagnostic.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The 11,602 residuals remain unexplained; no production selector change is authorized.
The shared-period phase-fold diagnostic run 43535760220 found that the 17-object subgroup has median coverage of 92/160 g bins and 91/160 r bins.
The 17 objects retain a positive common Table 2 period, both positive mean magnitudes and raw photometry in both bands.
The matched-control design uses one same-Type Table 4 member per residual, matched on common period, g/r magnitudes and Ng/Nr.

Chan et al. (2022), Section 2.1, specifies george MGPR, normalized phase/wavelength coordinates, separable RBF kernel, constant amplitude, diagonal white noise, zero mean, L-BFGS-B, three phase cycles and a 160-point output grid.
Workflow 43601683991 completed successfully on commit 886608da7154e8a4cea3f2d984b4c767baf97161 with 17 residuals and 17 matched Table4 controls.
Artifact 14117002862 passed all three workflow steps after checksum-pinned g/r archive retrieval and the bounded MGPR audit.

baseline.cohort: 17 candidate-only residuals with both mean magnitudes and one missing band-specific period; 17 deterministic matched Table 4 controls

change.proposed: Add a read-only, bounded MGPR feasibility diagnostic using george==0.4.4.
change.scope: Research-only script, tests and GitHub Actions workflow; no product dependencies, model, selector, feature schema, scientific threshold or baseline artifact changes.
change.rationale: The paper phase-folds both bands using the common Table 2 period. The 17 residuals have adequate observed phase coverage, so MGPR feasibility is the next discriminating experiment.

expected_improvement: Measure optimizer convergence and negative log likelihood for each residual and matched control.
Record fitted phase/wavelength length scales, kernel amplitude, diagonal white-noise variance and covariance condition number.
Generate 160-point posterior mean and uncertainty curves for each band.
Separate a successful numerical fit from scientific membership evidence.

The fitted wavelength metric hit its upper log bound in 6/17 residuals and 9/17 controls. Multi-start and bound sensitivity remain open.

Both raw archive hashes, decompressed member hashes, byte counts, row counts and CRCs passed integrity checks.

root_causes: The 17 residuals with both mean magnitudes and missing one band-specific period can be fitted by the bounded shared-period MGPR implementation; a missing Per-g or Per-r value is not a numerical MGPR blocker under this diagnostic.
The 11,602 CPVS membership discrepancy is not explained by MGPR convergence; historical membership decisions occur upstream or depend on additional undocumented selection/preparation stages.
limitations: This is a bounded diagnostic, not an exact reproduction of the authors' private code. The paper does not specify George version, initial values, bounds or the complete implementation.
Two starts per object are insufficient for optimization robustness: six objects have start-dependent likelihood gaps above 1, including large gaps.
Six residuals and nine controls have the wavelength metric at its upper optimizer bound.

All available rows were used to fit and assess the posterior. No held-out epochs, blocked time validation or independent interpolation validation was performed. Posterior sigma is not a generalization-error estimate.
The Zenodo g_flag/r_flag mapping to DR2 catflags remains unverified; all numerically valid rows were used without applying an unverified flag policy.
The successful fit does not establish catalogue membership or explain the remaining 11,602 IDs.

findings: The shared Table2 period supports a finite, converged two-band GP fit for all 17 examined residuals despite one missing band-specific period value.
Numerical MGPR feasibility does not prove that an object belongs to the published Table4 sample.
Posterior uncertainty and optimizer convergence must be separated from held-out predictive performance.
A two-start optimization can return successful fits while still showing material local-optimum sensitivity.

open_blockers: Extend deterministic multi-start testing to at least 8 starts per object and test sensitivity to optimizer bounds.
Compare posterior curves across converged starts, not only negative log likelihood.
Add blocked/held-out phase or epoch validation without using held-out rows in fitting.
Review objects whose wavelength metric reaches the upper bound and whose NLL changes materially across starts.
Rerun the robust MGPR audit on the latest branch head after the multi-start sensitivity changes.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not use MGPR convergence as a CPVS membership selector.
Do not change production code or the v0.2.0 baseline.
Treat the successful 34-object run as bounded numerical feasibility only.
Investigate multi-start sensitivity and held-out prediction before interpreting uncertainty metrics.
Continue reconstructing original Chen selection, flag semantics and full-parent object-level membership.
